precise_obstruction.claim: A physical meridian of the represented knot cannot be one of the attaching curves of an embedded doubly pointed diagram satisfying the current local definition.
precise_obstruction.proof: Let beta_j=boundary(D_j) be any beta attaching curve and take its supplied embedded compression disk D_j in U_beta. The beta arc is disjoint from D_j by Definition. The alpha arc lies in the other handlebody; its endpoints are w,z, neither on beta_j. Consequently D_j is a smooth spanning disk for beta_j disjoint from the entire represented knot K. Push its boundary slightly into its collar if needed, keeping it disjoint from K. Its algebraic intersection with K is zero, so lk(beta_j,K)=0. The same argument applies to every alpha attaching curve. A genuine oriented meridian of K has linking +1 or -1, hence cannot coincide with any such attaching curve as a curve in the physical knot exterior. This obstruction survives an orientation-preserving diagram isomorphism carrying the knot and disks.
precise_obstruction.consequence: An exterior splitting with a filling meridian mu is a valid different encoding, but its meridian filling disk meets the filling core once. It is not an embedded endpoint object in the local disk-disjoint arc convention with mu still the physical meridian. Applying the accepted endpoint invariance after abstract extraction does not identify the old physical meridian, its longitude replacement, or its capped Seifert generator field with the new embedded knot. Those extra comparisons are exactly what the absolute cap calculation requires.
